actions.action: Set the clear pot inside a heavier, wider ceramic or terracotta cachepot
Add a layer of pebbles or LECA to the bottom of the outer pot
Tuck smooth stones or pebbles into the bark or saucer around the pot
Reposition the stake closer to vertical and re-clip the spike
Put a silicone mat, shelf liner, or museum putty under the saucer
Move the plant to a corner or against a wall
Check the bark and roots and water only when the bark is mostly dry
Cut back the spike once the blooms fade

reason: The answer identifies top-heaviness and an unstable pot as the cause, its first and best fix (nesting the pot in a heavier outer pot) matches what worked, and nothing it recommends is harmful.
